newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Hyundai issuing US$300 mln bonds in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai issuing US$300 mln bonds in Asia.

text.p: Hyundai Group, South Korea's biggest conglomerate, soon will issue five-year corporate bonds in Asia to raise US$300 million worth of funds, lead underwriter Union Bank of Switzerland's Taipei branch said on Wednesday.
The plan includes a bond issue in Taiwan to raise US$50 million, a Union Bank executive in Taipei who declined to be identified told Reuters.
The executive would not disclose a date for the issues.
"Our bank has signed contracts with Hyundai to help it issue five-year bonds worth US$300 million in Asia, including US$50 million in Taiwan," the executive said by telephone.
The bonds will be set with a yield of LIBOR plus 60 basis points, the executive said.
The issues will be handled by the Hong Kong branch of Union Bank of Switzerland, he said.
Other details were yet to be made final, he said.
The executive said he was unaware of how Hyundai planned to use the finds.
Few international firms have turned to Taiwan for capital, although the multilateral Asian Development Bank has launched two Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds in Taiwan worth a total of US$355 million.

Taiwan has a goal of developing itself into an Asia-Pacific financial centre, with an initial aim is to become a funding centre by increasing the international accessibility and transparency of its huge capital base.
